vogue italia under franca sozzani was simply in a league of its own. vogue italia december 2009 ‘meiselpic’ by steven meisel

this piece had the supermodels, the attitude, the fun and the kind of creative direction that made fashion feel exciting. looking at it now, it’s almost wild how much personality and relevance a story can hold. the casting alone is insane [slide 19]

an editorial that still feels more relevant than half of what we see today.
nothing worse than an ugly copy 🤷🏻‍♀️ also disappointed but not surprised
its the slightly dirty feet on slide 2 that make this so wholesome

ai could never make a campaign this fun 💋steve madden’s big head girls ran from 1997 to mid 2000s.  the surreal, weird, bratty visuals still feels so cool. it was playful, instantly recognisable and yes iconic. can we get more fashion campaigns with this much personality???????
the blend is so satisfying, its fashion asmr

not only it sends a beautiful message, but the garments also look rather cool. these are the sort of concepts, narratives and perspectives that i still think are missing from fashion, especially when fashion right now is surviving on greenwashing, performative sustainability, activism and whatnot. it’s refreshing to see someone really putting it out there with such a strong message.

it’s just a beautiful way to make you really think about the hundred things that go behind making a shirt, a pair of trousers or a top. there’s so much human labour behind fashion that we simply don’t see. kudos to this brand for making that impossible to ignore.

i came across this brand years ago and it genuinely stayed with me. so, some time back, i decided to reach out and learn more about their process because i was fascinated by what i had seen.

one of the greatest fashion editorials ever, honestly. this 2006 vogue story featuring kirsten dunst as marie antoinette is pure visual perfection. photographed by annie leibovitz at versailles, with immaculate styling, incredible locations and the kind of storytelling that makes every frame feel like a painting. even as a film promotion, the execution is just ridiculously beautiful.

Often underrated but this collection is Galliano to the very core. John Galliano fall 1995. Dolores del Rio. Sailors. Ship. Flamenco. Bias. Ruffles. Snow.
what do we think??? also why is masimo here? what did i miss?

with the JG met gala announcement, i can’t stop thinking about galliano’s personal style. not just his legendary collections, but the way he dressed himself. chaotic, theatrical, impossible to forget. fashion feels a little less magical without people who dress like they’re the main character.

ps bring back personal style.

@briandecarvalho reveals the real story behind his viral razor blade dress, and why it was born out of frustration after years of being asked to lend his work for free. In this clip from Speaking of Fashion, hosted by @brownfashiongal, he shares how the piece became a statement about creativity, boundaries, and knowing the value of your work.

Full episode on our youtube

home office core by @savingshivvy feels especially relevant at a time when layoffs, burnout and impossible expectations have become part of everyday working life. from endless zoom calls to the pressure of always being available, work has quietly seeped into every corner of our lives. through reconstruction, satire and familiar cultural symbols, the london and seoul-based designer behind saving shivvy captures the absurdity of modern work culture.
